{{Short description|None}}
'''Advanced statistics''', also known as '''analytics''' or '''APBRmetrics''', in [[basketball]] refers to the analysis of [[basketball statistics]] using objective evidence.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/stats/help/faq|title=NBA.com/Stats Frequently Asked Questions|website=NBA.com}}</ref> APBRmetrics takes its name from the acronym APBR, which stands for the Association for Professional Basketball Research.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbastuffer.com/analytics101/apbrmetrics/|title=APBRmetrics - NBAstuffer|date=May 8, 2017|website=www.nbastuffer.com}}</ref> According to ''The Sporting News'', the APBRmetrics message board was "the birthplace of basketball analytics".<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/nba-twitter-stats-analytics-message-board-basketball/takw7w6zbj7ntzdm92stqg2f|title=The birthplace of basketball analytics: Before the chaos of NBA Twitter, one message board quietly kicked off a stats revolution|date=November 18, 2022|website=www.sportingnews.com}}</ref>

Advanced basketball statistics include [[effective field goal percentage]] (eFG%), [[true shooting percentage]] (TS%), on-court/off-court [[Plus–minus (sports)#Basketball|plus–minus]], [[Adjusted Plus Minus|adjusted plus-minus]] (APM), real plus/minus (RPM), [[player efficiency rating]] (PER), [[offense efficiency rating]], [[offensive rating]], [[defensive rating]], [[similarity score]], [[tendex]], and [[Player tracking (National Basketball Association)|player tracking]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.northwestern.edu/nusportsanalytics/2020/12/22/an-introduction-to-advanced-basketball-statistics-individual-statistics/|title=An Introduction to Advanced Basketball Statistics: Individual Statistics – Northwestern Sports Analytics Group|website=sites.northwestern.edu}}</ref> A more complete explanation of basketball analytics is available in "A Starting Point for Analyzing Basketball Statistics" in the ''Journal of Quantitative Analysis in Sports''.<ref>{{cite journal |url=http://www.bepress.com/jqas/vol3/iss3/1 |author=Kubatko, Justin |author2=Oliver, Dean |author3=Pelton, Kevin |author4=Rosenbaum, Dan T |name-list-style=amp |year=2007 |title=A Starting Point for Analyzing Basketball Statistics |journal=Journal of Quantitative Analysis in Sports |volume=3 |issue=3 (Article 1) |doi=10.2202/1559-0410.1070 |s2cid=121583997 |access-date=2007-10-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071226165154/http://www.bepress.com/jqas/vol3/iss3/1/ |archive-date=2007-12-26 |url-status=dead |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Notable basketball analytics practitioners==
The field of basketball analytics practitioners includes, but is not limited to, the following individuals:

* [[Martin Manley]] wrote Basketball Heaven. Created Player Efficiency metric and many other advanced metrics.  
* [[John Hollinger]] authored four books in the ''Pro Basketball Forecast/Prospectus'' series and was a regular columnist for ESPN Insider. He is a former vice president of basketball operations for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].

* Justin Kubatko created and maintained the website Basketball-Reference.com, the professional basketball arm of [[Sports Reference]] LLC, until 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://statitudes.com/blog/2013/08/20/hello-goodbye/|title=Hello, Goodbye|website=Statitudes.com|access-date=2017-08-09|archive-date=2017-08-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809090302/http://statitudes.com/blog/2013/08/20/hello-goodbye/|url-status=dead}}</ref> During Kubatko's tenure, Sports Reference was named one of the 50 best websites of 2010 by ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.time.com/time/specials/packages/article/0,28804,2012721_2012880_2012751,00.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100827000824/http://www.time.com/time/specials/packages/article/0,28804,2012721_2012880_2012751,00.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 27, 2010|title=50 Best Websites 2010|date=25 August 2010|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|access-date=2017-08-09}}</ref>
 
* [[Dean Oliver (statistician)|Dean Oliver]], "one of the godfathers of NBA analytics",<ref name="auto"/> is a former [[NCAA Division III]] player and assistant coach at [[Caltech Beavers|Caltech]]. He is also a scout who has consulted with the Seattle SuperSonics, and served in the front office of the [[Denver Nuggets]] and the Sacramento Kings.
